name: Quiet Oaks RV Park
note: RV park at 13129 FM 346, Bullard (East Texas, ~15 min S of Tyler, near Lake Palestine). Full-hookup sites for 30/50-amp rigs, free WiFi; overnight, weekly, and monthly stays, book by phone. RV Life 4.5*/$$ (9.0/10, auto 7/2026). --Claude

name: Republic RV Park
note: Private RV park on US-281 in George West (Live Oak County), South Texas. Full-hookup sites with WiFi from ~$27/night; nightly transient bookings (book by phone). Well kept per reviews (owner attention to detail). RV Life 4.5*/$$ over 21 reviews (auto 7/2026). --Claude

name: South Fork 82 RV Park
note: Newly built RV park near Blossom in far NE Texas (Lamar County). Full-hookup sites, some covered, for short or long stays; online booking via operator site. --Claude

name: W. Lee Colburn Park (Elm Creek Reservoir)
note: City of Winters park on Elm Creek Reservoir (Lake Winters); 14 RV sites with 30A electric + water on gravel/grass, dump station, boat ramp and fishing pier. First-come, first-served / pay at park. --Claude

name: Wichita Bend RV Park
note: City of Wichita Falls-run 28-space RV park on the east bank of the Wichita River near the Texas Travel Information Center, adjacent to Lucy Park via a swinging pedestrian bridge. Water + electric (all 30-amp, 14 sites also 50-amp), no sewer but dump station on site; no restrooms so self-contained rigs only. First-come, first-served, $17/night, 72-hr max per two weeks. --Claude

name: Bottomless Lakes State Park (Lea Lake Campground)
note: Lea Lake campground at New Mexico's first state park; ~32 developed sites on the SW shore of Lea Lake including 25 pull-through sites with 30/50-amp electric + water (7 also sewer), restrooms w/ showers and a dump station. Electric sites reservable via ReserveAmerica; overflow/other sites first-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Rockhound State Park Campground
note: Rockhound State Park campground on the flank of the Little Florida Mountains SE of Deming; 29 sites including 23 with 30-amp electric+water on large level gravel pads with sheltered tables, dump station, restrooms w/ showers. A handful of electric sites reservable via ReserveAmerica, remainder first-come, first-served. --Claude

name: City of Rocks State Park Campground
note: City of Rocks State Park near Faywood; ~50 sites tucked among the volcanic rock formations, including 10 sites with 30-amp electric+water (a couple reservable online, the rest first-come, first-served) plus many FCFS non-electric sites, dump station and restrooms. --Claude

name: Valley of Fires Recreation Area (BLM)
note: BLM Valley of Fires Recreation Area, 4 mi W of Carrizozo on US-380, on the Carrizozo Malpais lava flow; 25 sites including 13 with 30/50-amp electric+water on a paved loop, sheltered tables, shower house w/ flush toilets, dump station. Mostly first-come, first-served; a few individual sites reservable on Recreation.gov. --Claude

name: Elephant Butte Lake State Park (Lions Beach Campground)
note: Lions Beach campground at Elephant Butte Lake State Park; 44 developed sites on terraced benches set back above the shoreline, with covered concrete pull-through pads carrying electric+water (some full-hookup), restrooms w/ showers; B-loop sites are advertised as overlooking the lake. Electric sites reservable Mar 1-Sep 30 via ReserveAmerica, otherwise first-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Santa Rosa Lake State Park — Rocky Point Campground
note: Rocky Point is the main developed campground at Santa Rosa Lake SP (Pecos River reservoir), on high ground near the dam. Two loops: Loop A has ~13 sites with water + 30/50-amp electric (RVs to ~50 ft), Loop B is dry (no hookups). Modern restrooms w/ showers, ADA sites, dump station. Mix of reservable (ReserveAmerica) and FCFS. Elev ~4,880 ft. --Claude

name: Ute Lake State Park
note: State park on Ute Lake (Canadian River reservoir) near Logan; main developed campground is a large loop of pull-through/back-in RV pads on a bench above the lake, plus North and Windy Point areas. ~146 sites park-wide (92 with water + 30/50-amp electric), RVs to ~70 ft; restrooms, showers, dump station, marina and boat ramps. Reservable via ReserveAmerica + FCFS. --Claude

name: Leasburg Dam State Park
note: Small developed campground on a bench above the Rio Grande ~15 mi N of Las Cruces. 24 sites: 12 with water + 30-amp, 4 with water + 50-amp, plus dry developed sites; concrete pads to ~40 ft, distinctive adobe-shade ramadas, restrooms w/ showers, dump station near the visitor center. Reservable (ReserveAmerica) + FCFS. Year-round. --Claude

name: Bluewater Lake State Park
note: Large high-elevation state park (~7,400 ft) on Bluewater Lake. ~149 developed sites across several campgrounds (Northpoint, Canyonside, Lakeside, Piñon Cliffs) plus Upper/Lower Electric loops (~14 sites, 30/50-amp, paved pads and pavilions). Restrooms w/ showers, vault toilets, dump station. About half reservable (ReserveAmerica), half FCFS. --Claude

name: Santa Rosa Lake State Park — Juniper Park Campground
note: Juniper is the lakeside campground at Santa Rosa Lake SP, closer to the water and boat ramp than Rocky Point; dry camping (no hookups) with picnic tables, fire rings/grills, water spigots and vault toilets. Drive-in RV-capable sites. FCFS/reservable via ReserveAmerica. Companion loop to Rocky Point. --Claude

name: Oasis State Park
note: Oasis SP N of Portales on the Llano Estacado — a shaded, dune-and-cottonwood oasis with a small stocked fishing pond. ~28-29 developed sites: ~14 water+electric (30/50-amp), 2 full-hookup, plus water-only sites; pull-through sites, showers, restrooms, dump station. Reservable (ReserveAmerica, 'Indian Grass Electric' loop) + FCFS. Year-round. --Claude

name: Storrie Lake State Park
note: Developed campground on the west shore of Storrie Lake just N of Las Vegas, NM (~6,600 ft). ~45 sites including a South Loop with ~13-22 water+electric (30-amp) sites, RVs to ~40 ft, plus a large primitive beach camping area. Restrooms w/ showers (winterized Oct-Apr), dump station, boat ramp, playground. Reservable (ReserveAmerica) + FCFS. --Claude

name: Chosa Campground (BLM)
note: BLM camping area between Carlsbad Caverns (~11 mi N) and Guadalupe Mountains NP; a large fenced ~3.5-acre gravel pad off CR 424 (Dillahunty Rd) that easily fits several big rigs and is nearly level. No hookups, no water, no restrooms; trash dumpster and primitive fire rings. First-come, first-served, 14-day limit — popular boondocking staging area for the two parks. --Claude

name: Clayton Lake State Park
note: NM State Park on ~170-acre Clayton Lake; 26 developed sites across five small campgrounds — 9 with water+30-amp electric, 7 water-only, rest primitive — plus pull-through RV sites, showers, dump station, boat ramp. Reservable online or FCFS. --Claude

name: Sunset Reef Campground
note: BLM campground (Carlsbad Field Office) on a reclaimed well pad off Washington Ranch Rd, ~14 mi S of Carlsbad Caverns; 11 developed sites — 5 for larger RVs plus tent/van spaces, shaded tables, fire rings, one vault toilet, no potable water. First-come, first-served, 5-night limit. --Claude

name: Pancho Villa State Park
note: NM State Park at Columbus on the US-Mexico border (1916 raid site) with a botanical/historic theme; ~79 developed sites — North Loop reservable (30 electric 30-amp, 5 50-amp, water throughout) plus South Loop 19 FCFS electric sites, level gravel pads to ~50 ft, dump station, showers. Reservable online + walk-up. --Claude

name: Villanueva State Park
note: NM State Park along the Pecos River amid red/yellow sandstone cliffs; 36 developed sites (12 with electric); the lower campground holds the hookup/RV sites and the upper campground is also RV-usable, rigs to ~40 ft; water, showers, dump station. Mix of reservable + FCFS, year-round with seasonal site rotation. --Claude

name: Percha Dam State Park
note: State park below Percha Diversion Dam on the Rio Grande; ~50 developed sites, 30 with electric (some pull-through with water), shaded by large cottonwoods, plus showers and a dump station. Accommodates all RV sizes; a noted birding spot. Reservable via ReserveAmerica (some FCFS). --Claude

name: Hyde Memorial State Park
note: New Mexico's oldest state park, in a Sangre de Cristo canyon ~8 mi NE of Santa Fe at ~8,500 ft; ~50 sites total with 7 electric (30-amp) sites along the canyon road for RVs, plus vault/flush toilets. Narrow canyon sites — larger rigs should scout. ReserveAmerica lists 37 of the campsites as bookable, the electric RV area included (read 2026-10-20). --Claude

name: Conchas Lake State Park
note: Reservoir state park on the Canadian River; developed north-side loops (Bell Point with adobe shade shelters, North Area, Cove) offer ~24 reservable + 9 FCFS water+electric (30-amp) sites plus water-only and primitive shoreline camping, with a dump station. Reservable via ReserveAmerica; many sites FCFS. --Claude

name: Elephant Butte Lake State Park, Desert Cove Campground
note: Elephant Butte Lake SP campground off Sumac Rd near the visitor center/marina; 16 developed sites with electric+water hookups, RVs to ~40 ft, fire ring/grill/table, showers and dump station. Electric sites reservable Mar 1-Sep 30 via ReserveAmerica, otherwise FCFS. --Claude

name: Coyote Creek State Park
note: NM state park in the Sangre de Cristos along Coyote Creek; ~38 developed sites incl 11 electric (30-amp) and 5 new full-hookup lean-to sites (50-amp) in the 2026 Aserradero loop, plus North Meadow/North End loops; electric + shared water, dump station. Drive-in, reservable via ReserveAmerica with some FCFS. --Claude

name: Orilla Verde Recreation Area - Rio Bravo Campground
note: BLM Orilla Verde area on the Rio Grande (Rio Grande del Norte NM); Rio Bravo has ~4 pull-through RV sites with water and electric (50-amp, no sewer) sitting close to the river, plus primitive sites; developed RV site $15/night, flush toilets/showers nearby. Individual sites are first-come, first-served (only the group shelter is reservable on recreation.gov). --Claude

name: Aguirre Spring Campground
note: BLM campground on the E side of the Organ Mountains; 55 FCFS sites, no hookups/water. Mostly short walk-in tent parking, but some roadside/pull-in sites fit a rig up to BLM's 23-ft recommended max - the 5.5-mi access road is steep, narrow and winding, so 23 ft is the limit and it's not for big rigs. --Claude

name: Orilla Verde Recreation Area - Pilar Campground
note: BLM Orilla Verde area on the Rio Grande; Pilar has ~9 pull-through RV sites with water and electric (50-amp, no sewer) and flush toilets; more private and set back from the water than riverside Rio Bravo; developed RV site $15/night. Individual sites are first-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Arroyo Hondo Campground (Orilla Verde Rec Area)
note: BLM Rio Grande del Norte NM / Orilla Verde Rec Area campground on NM-570 along the Rio Grande. 5 drive-in sites on the riverbank, each with table, fire ring and grill; drinking water and vault toilets; no shade shelters. Best for tents but sites also accommodate trailers/small RVs. First-come, first-served (individual sites not reservable). --Claude

name: Juniper Campground - Bandelier National Monument
note: NPS campground on the mesa near the Bandelier entrance station. Three loops (Abert's Squirrel FCFS, Black Bear reservable year-round, Coyote reservable Mar-Oct); no hookups, max RV length 36 ft with only a handful of sites over 30 ft. Flush toilets, potable water. Mix of reservable and first-come sites. --Claude

name: Cosmic Campground
note: Gila NF (Glenwood RD) primitive campground 8 mi N of Alma off US-180 — first Intl Dark Sky Sanctuary on National Forest land. 8 sites incl 6 concrete RV pads to 32 ft, picnic tables + fire rings, pit toilet, NO potable water. First-come, first-served (not on recreation.gov). --Claude

name: Mesa Campground (Lake Roberts)
note: Gila NF (Wilderness RD) campground on a mesa above Lake Roberts ~25 mi N of Mimbres on NM-35. 24 sites, 12 with water+electric; flush toilets, potable water; most sites to 32 ft, 2 to 40 ft. First-come, first-served (not on recreation.gov). --Claude

name: Sapillo Campground (Gila NF)
note: Undeveloped, primitive Gila NF camping area under ponderosa pines ~15 mi north of Mimbres off NM-35, near Sapillo Creek/CDNST trailhead. No defined numbered sites — ample level parking, one vault toilet, no potable water; gravel/dirt drive-in accessible to a small RV. Popular with group campers but open FCFS to all; 14-day limit. --Claude

name: Pinon Campground (Quemado Lake, Gila NF)
note: Gila NF campground across from Juniper CG, ~1.4 mi from Quemado Lake off NM-103/FR-13. 23 individual sites (+2 group shelters), some large enough for self-contained RVs to ~35 ft; vault toilets, grills, RV dump station ($15), seasonal water mid-May-Sep, no hookups. Individual sites FCFS, group sites reservable online. Fishing/boating at Quemado Lake. --Claude

name: McGaffey Campground (Cibola NF)
note: Cibola NF campground in the Zuni Mountains, ~8 mi south of Fort Wingate on SR-400 (Exit 33 off I-40), at ~7,800 ft near McGaffey Lake. 29 drive-in sites plus 3 group sites and picnic area; vault toilets, no hookups or potable water, open seasonally mid-May-Sep. The FS page's 'trailers under 22 ft' is a conservative turnaround caveat — Campendium reviewers report level sites fitting rigs to ~40 ft. Individual sites FCFS; group sites reservable. --Claude

name: Rio de las Vacas Campground
note: Santa Fe NF campground along the Rio de las Vacas near the San Pedro Parks Wilderness, Cuba Ranger District (~8,250 ft). 15 sites with paved RV pads on paved roads, vault toilets and a camp host; sites 1-11 reservable via Recreation.gov, 4 first-come, first-served. (Closed Jul 7-Aug 7 2026 for road repaving.) --Claude

name: Agua Piedra Campground
note: Carson NF campground on NM-518 in the upper Rio Pueblo canyon (Camino Real RD), ~44 sites across a Lower loop plus Loop A and Loop B; standard nonelectric (no hookups), vault toilets. Individual sites are first-come, first-served; the two group shelters are reservable online. Per-site max RV lengths run ~25-36 ft, so it fits a 23-ft rig. Near the Rio Pueblo and Agua Piedra Creek (trout fishing). --Claude

name: Holy Ghost Campground
note: Santa Fe NF campground in Holy Ghost Canyon along Holy Ghost Creek, 16 mi N of Pecos via NM-63 then FR 122; 23 single sites, vault toilets, no potable water, no hookups. First-come, first-served (the separate Holy Ghost Group Area is reservable online). Opens roughly mid-May to mid-Oct; reopened and operating after the 2022 Hermits Peak/Calf Canyon fire. FR 122 is narrow — trailers over ~25 ft not advised, so a 23-ft rig fits. --Claude
